name: vscode-litellm
description: Route GitHub Copilot chat, completions, inline suggestions, and agents through your LiteLLM proxy.

commands.title: LiteLLM Proxy: Store API Key Securely
LiteLLM Proxy: Clear Stored API Key

vscode-litellm.enabled.markdownDescription: Master switch. When enabled, Copilot's chat/completions endpoints are redirected to `#vscode-litellm.proxyBaseUrl#`. Disabling restores the real GitHub endpoints.

vscode-litellm.proxyBaseUrl.markdownDescription: Base URL of the LiteLLM proxy (no trailing slash), e.g. `http://localhost:4000`.

vscode-litellm.defaultDeployment.markdownDescription: Optional. Single LiteLLM model name used in the exported config for any Copilot model that has no explicit entry in `#vscode-litellm.modelMap#` (e.g. `openai/gpt-4o`). Leave empty to export identity mappings.

vscode-litellm.modelMap.markdownDescription: Maps Copilot model names (what the picker sends) to LiteLLM model names. Edit with the *LiteLLM Proxy: Configure Model Map* command. Names observed during the spike should be added here.

vscode-litellm.deployment.apiBase.markdownDescription: Optional. Written as `api_base` for every deployment in the exported config.yml.

vscode-litellm.deployment.apiKey.markdownDescription: Optional. Written as `api_key` for every deployment in the exported config.yml. Stored in plain text — prefer an env var name like `OS.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY']` for sensitive setups.

vscode-litellm.forwarder.enabled.markdownDescription: Run a local auth-rewriting forwarder (`127.0.0.1:forwarder.port`) in front of the proxy. Needed when the proxy enforces an API key — Copilot sends its own ephemeral Copilot JWT, which key-checked proxies reject. When enabled, Copilot's override keys point at the forwarder, not directly at the proxy.

vscode-litellm.forwarder.apiKey.markdownDescription: API key sent to the proxy as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Falls back to `#vscode-litellm.deployment.apiKey#` when empty. Stored in plain text — prefer **LiteLLM Proxy: Store API Key Securely** (SecretStorage), which takes priority while set.

vscode-litellm.forwarder.requestTimeoutM.markdownDescription: Milliseconds to wait for the upstream proxy's first response byte before the forwarder gives up (then retries once, or answers 504). `0` disables the timeout. Long-running SSE streams are NOT cut off — only the wait for the first byte is bounded.

vscode-litellm.forwarder.fallbackModel.markdownDescription: Model ID used when the requested model is unavailable. When the upstream refuses a request with a model-not-found error (404 / 400 “model does not exist”), the forwarder retries it once with this model. Requires `#vscode-litellm.forwarder.enabled#`.

vscode-litellm.surfaces.chat.markdownDescription: Route chat (CAPI base: chat, responses, messages, embeddings) through the proxy.

vscode-litellm.surfaces.agents.markdownDescription: Route agent/skill surfaces (CAPI base: /agents, /skills, /search) through the proxy.

vscode-litellm.surfaces.completions.markdownDescription: Route code completions (proxy base) through the proxy.

vscode-litellm.statusPollIntervalMs.markdownDescription: How often the status bar pings the endpoint (health + model list). Values below 5000 are clamped to 5000.

vscode-litellm.logLevel.markdownDescription: Minimum level written to the `vscode-litellm` output channel (View → Output → "vscode-litellm"). `trace` (default) logs every forwarded request/response, including the 30s status poll; `info` is quieter. `fatal` (unhandled exceptions) is always logged.

vscode-litellm.surfaces.nes.markdownDescription: Route inline hints / Next Edit Suggestions (proxy base) through the proxy.
